stem.text: Let \( f(x) = - 4 \left(x - 2\right) \cos{\left(\frac{1}{x - 2} \right)} + 1 \) for \( x \ne 2 \). Find \( \lim_{x \to 2} f(x) \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: The limit is 1, because \( 1 - 4 \left|{x - 2}\right| \le f(x) \le 4 \left|{x - 2}\right| + 1 \) for \( x \ne 2 \) and both bounds approach 1 as x approaches 2.

worked_solution.text: Multiplying by the nonnegative quantity \( 4 \left|{x - 2}\right| \) and adding 1 gives \( 1 - 4 \left|{x - 2}\right| \le f(x) \le 4 \left|{x - 2}\right| + 1 \). The factor \( - 4 \left(x - 2\right) \) can be negative, so its absolute value is used to keep the inequality true.
Both bounds are continuous, so their limits as x approaches 2 are both 1.

options.label: The limit is 1, because \( 1 - 4 \left|{x - 2}\right| \le f(x) \le 4 \left|{x - 2}\right| + 1 \) for \( x \ne 2 \) and both bounds approach 1 as x approaches 2.
The limit is 1, because \( 4 \left(x - 2\right) + 1 \le f(x) \le - 4 \left(x - 2\right) + 1 \) for \( x \ne 2 \) and both bounds approach 1 as x approaches 2.
options.derivation: the bounds of the oscillating factor multiplied by the sign changing factor without reversing the inequality where it is negative

options.label: The limit is 1, because \( - 4 \left(x - 2\right) \) approaches 0 and \( \cos{\left(\frac{1}{x - 2} \right)} \) approaches a limit as x approaches 2, so the product theorem applies.
options.derivation: the product limit theorem used although its hypothesis fails, since the oscillating factor has no limit
